candidate_policy.observed_text:
For planning removal of an inner-race bearing, the machine and mounting information needed includes: the machine/equipment identity and configuration; shaft and housing dimensions, fits, and tolerances; bearing designation, type, and mounting arrangement (including whether it is mounted on an adapter sleeve or with interference fit); the location and accessibility of the bearing; adjacent components and any locking devices; the required removal direction and available space; the condition of the shaft/housing surfaces; and any manufacturer-specific removal instructions. The teaching material (SRC-K01-02, generic bearing education) can describe general principles and typical sequences for removal, but it cannot select a specific removal force or heating temperature for the unidentified equipment. Those values depend on model-specific data, fits, materials, and manufacturer procedures that are not supplied. The scenario assumption of shaft-housing misalignment during mounting is a teaching assumption, not an observed cause, and does not authorize any specific removal parameter.
No actual device records, model-specific thresholds, or manufacturer removal specifications were supplied.
The source is registered generic bearing education (SRC-K01-02); it does not authorize model-specific or aviation/reuse decisions.
The assumed cause (shaft-housing misalignment during mounting) is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observation or classifier inference.
The historical online reading was not observed or reconstructed in this review; the saved PDF's byte-identity to the historical reading is machine-unresolved.
Visual review covered only pages 2, 5, 18, 19, and 24, not all 24 pages.
No removal force or heating temperature can be substantiated for the unidentified equipment from the available context.
